clue.text: Clergy overhauls the masses, for instance

definitions.note: plural definition matching a plural answer

parts.note: the church can mean the clergy as a body
a car's services are its overhauls or routine maintenance checks

explanation.surface: A clergyman giving the general public a thorough going-over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The masses' looks like the common people, but here it is the Catholic rite in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mass is one example of a formal act of worship held in a parish.

clue.text: Listened to the sound of the cows

indicators.note: the sound of tells us to take a word as it is spoken, not spelt

parts.note: a group of cows is a herd

explanation.surface: Someone attended to the lowing of the cattle.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of hear, the verb for taking in noise with the ears.

clue.text: Island with lots of sound streets

indicators.note: sound asks for a word spoken the same as a word for streets

parts.note: streets are roads

explanation.surface: An island boasting plenty of well-built streets.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound' looks like an adjective meaning solid; it is the homophone signal. RHODES is a Greek island in the Aegean.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhodes is a Greek island in the Dodecanese group.

clue.text: Somersault of the workers' principal with initial gyration

parts.note: hands are manual workers, as in farmhands
prin. is a dictionary abbreviation for principal

indicators.note: initial tells us to take only the opening letter of the word gyration

explanation.surface: A gymnastic flip performed by the head of the labour force, spinning round at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: PRIN is a less familiar abbreviation of principal; G is the first letter of gyration.
explanation.definitionFit: A handspring is a gymnastic flip in which the body turns over onto the hands and back to the feet.

clue.text: Was he know as the 'whirlwind'?

parts.note: a nickname for a man reads instead as a swirling current, a common noun that is also a boy's name

explanation.surface: Asking whether a man went by the nickname Whirlwind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Know' is printed for 'known'. The clue reads as a sporting nickname, but the answer is a man's first name that is also a word for a swirling current.
explanation.definitionFit: A small whirlpool or whirlwind of air or water is the common-noun sense; it is also a pet name for Edward.

clue.text: Shake whippersnapper in fight

indicators.note: in tells us one word sits inside the other

parts.note: to vie is to compete or fight
a whippersnapper is an impudent youngster, a brat

explanation.surface: A cheeky youngster gets shaken up in a scrap.
explanation.definitionFit: To vibrate is to quiver or tremble rapidly.

clue.text: Prisoner's swindle to steal

parts.note: a con is a convict, a prisoner
to diddle is to cheat or swindle

explanation.surface: A convict's scam to make off with someone's property.
explanation.walkthrough: CONDIDDLE is a rare Scots word for pilfering.
explanation.definitionFit: An old Scots verb meaning to pilfer or make off with something.

clue.text: Send gun dog with beater to a forced get-together

indicators.note: a beater stirs and whisks, so it signals the preceding letters are beaten into a new order

explanation.surface: A shooting party: send out the gun dog along with the beater.
explanation.walkthrough: A beater on a shoot drives game towards the guns, so it sits naturally beside 'gun dog'; here it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A marriage hurried through because the bride is pregnant, as though at gunpoint.

clue.text: I sully precious process disdainfully

indicators.note: to process material is to work it over into a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone sneeringly spoils a treasured procedure.
explanation.definitionFit: Supercilious means haughtily contemptuous, so the adverb describes acting with scorn.

clue.text: Terribly rude donna is not dressed!

indicators.note: terribly suggests the letters are mangled into a new order

explanation.surface: An outraged remark that a rude prima donna has turned up undressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Unadorned means plain, without decoration or trimming.

clue.text: Brian's good, odd-numbered game

indicators.note: odd-numbered means take the first, third, fifth letters and so on of the words

explanation.surface: Brian is skilled at a game with odd numbers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Odd-numbered' suggests the numbers called in the game, but it picks letters 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9 of 'Brian's good'.
explanation.definitionFit: Bingo is a numbers game where players mark off called figures.

clue.text: Incessant aim to be younger

parts.note: an end is an aim or goal
being younger means having less age, so the clue supplies the comparative word less

explanation.surface: A never-ending wish to grow young again.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is loose: to be younger is to be 'less' in years.
explanation.definitionFit: Endless means without stopping or limit.

clue.text: Looking after ones saloon, for example, in the Gabon

parts.note: a saloon is a type of car, here one's own
G is the international vehicle registration code for Gabon

explanation.surface: Tending one's car while out in the African state of Gabon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ones' stands for 'one's'. A saloon is a British car body style (a sedan); Gabon is a country in west-central Africa.
explanation.definitionFit: Caring is tending or looking after someone or something.

clue.text: Torrential rain causes rivers to protrude

parts.note: waters can mean rivers or seas
to pout is to push the lips out, to protrude

explanation.surface: A downpour making rivers burst their banks.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides a sea whirlwind, the word can mean a sudden heavy downpour.

clue.text: First cot's ready inside bedroom

indicators.note: first tells us to take the opening letter of each following word

explanation.surface: A baby's first cot is set up in the bedroom.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening letters of the last four words spell the answer, while the whole clue describes it.
explanation.definitionFit: A crib is a baby's cot, the kind set up in a nursery.

clue.text: Without preparation I'm going to prod you soundly

parts.note: I'm without its apostrophe
to prompt is to prod or nudge

indicators.note: soundly tells us to take the letter that is spoken like the word you

parts.note: said aloud, these words sound like U

explanation.surface: Someone announcing they will give another a firm poke on the spur of the moment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soundly' looks like 'thoroughly'; it signals the letter U, said like 'you'.
explanation.definitionFit: Impromptu means done on the spur of the moment, unrehearsed.

clue.text: Provide a weapon to old fellow for the final struggle

parts.note: to arm someone is to give them a weapon
aged means old
a don is a university fellow

explanation.surface: Arming an elderly academic for the last battle.
explanation.definitionFit: In Revelation, the last battle between good and evil at the end of the world.

clue.text: Madly pedal about hinge extending over the edges

indicators.note: about tells us the scrambled letters go round the other piece
madly signals the letters of pedal are scrambled

parts.note: a hinge is a kind of joint

explanation.surface: Frantically pedalling around on a hinge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Madly' scrambles the cyclist's word into LAPED, and 'about' wraps that round the hinge word; 'pedal' looks like part of a bicycle scene but is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A lap joint is made by overlapping two pieces, so lap-jointed parts overlap one another.

clue.text: Making public, personal information about son's sacking

indicators.note: about tells us the first piece wraps round the next

parts.note: outing is exposing private facts about someone, especially sexuality
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: Revealing private details about a boy led to his dismissal.
explanation.definitionFit: Ousting someone is removing them from a post, like a dismissal.

clue.text: Pitney's hereditary determinant

definitions.meaning: first name of the American pop singer Pitney
the unit of heredity carried on a chromosome

explanation.surface: A singer's inherited trait.
explanation.definitionFit: Pitney the 1960s singer had this first name, and it is also the unit of DNA passing traits to offspring.

clue.text: Sketch of French emblem

parts.note: de is French for of
a sign is a symbol or emblem

explanation.surface: A drawing of a French badge.
explanation.definitionFit: A design is a drawing or plan, a sketch.

clue.text: Ordinary male address for premier musician

parts.note: bo is an American way of addressing a man, like buddy
premier means first, written 1ST, read as IST

explanation.surface: A man's ordinary speech to the leading performer.
explanation.walkthrough: Premier gives 1ST, with the figure 1 standing in for the letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: An oboist plays the oboe, an orchestral woodwind instrument.

clue.text: Directed deer set running

indicators.note: running suggests the letters are on the move and rearranged

explanation.surface: A herd of deer is driven to run.
explanation.definitionFit: Steered means guided or directed on a course.

clue.text: Build beams, say

indicators.note: say tells us the word is taken as spoken

parts.note: beams of light are rays

explanation.surface: Putting up beams in a building, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests roof beams in construction; here beams are rays of light.
explanation.definitionFit: To raise a structure is to erect or construct it.

clue.text: Argue over some thoughtless parking

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Two people quarrel about inconsiderate parking.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to argue or dispute with someone.

clue.text: Very good Greek character joins shah of Persia

parts.note: so is used for very, as in so good
phi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An excellent Greek figure joins the Persian ruler.
explanation.walkthrough: SOPHI (also Sophy) is an old title for the ruler of Persia.
explanation.definitionFit: An archaic title given to the ruler of the Safavid dynasty in Persia.

clue.text: Preparation for a dream

parts.note: pro means for or in favour of
a vision is a dream or imagined sight

explanation.surface: Getting ready for something one has dreamed of.
explanation.definitionFit: Making provision is arranging things in advance.

clue.text: Grandson of James II urged open-entry reform

indicators.note: to reform is to form again, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A grandson of a king pressed for reform to open up entry.
explanation.walkthrough: The nickname of Charles Edward Stuart, who tried to retake the British throne in 1745.
explanation.definitionFit: Bonnie Prince Charlie, claimant to the British crown, was the grandson of James II.
